answer: At every drill the coxswain calls the lifeboat crew by name and signs the muster roll, and only a crew that answers the roll may launch. A beacon name called from the crowd fails the roll: the basalt of the boat must hold the men the coxswain trained, and a stranger cannot pull an oar in time. Faking the crew means training twelve men for a year, running 40 drills and paying 13,500, while the signal signature on the roll is checked before every launch, so a name that was never mustered is left on the shore.
